title: Investigation assistant
scope: Checks use the facts and links you enter. Free text is not interpreted. Unspecified facts remain unknown.
crimeHint: Define what really happened, why, who was involved and under what circumstances. Add people, places, events and evidence here or use your existing nodes.
matrixHint: Write the conclusions players can draw. Link each clue to a conclusion and explain why it supports or refutes it. Disputed clues can create suspicion, but do not establish a fact.
timelineHint: Use separate periods for different nights or historical cases. Enter times as HH:mm or day/HH:mm (1/02:16 = the next day). A range means the start time is uncertain; duration is in minutes. Confirmed alibis participate in the same checks as events.
reachabilityHint: Choose actual player entry points and endings. All prerequisites in one discovery method are required; separate methods are alternatives. Diagram branches alone do not make clues discoverable.
deadEndsHint: Review branches with no useful outcome and clues whose loss blocks the ending. Add an alternative discovery method or an independent clue in the previous steps.
versionsHint: A convincing false version needs a motive, an apparent supporting clue and a discoverable refutation. Suggestions combine the motives and evidence you entered; review them before adding.
completenessHint: Check existing investigations here too. Recommendations do not prevent saving a draft. A clean report covers structured facts only; it cannot guarantee that narrative prose has no contradictions.
name: Name
clueLocations: Places where players should find clues
clueAdvice: Aim for at least three different clues in each selected place. Fewer clues are allowed. Adding multiple roles to one clue still counts as one clue.
period: Period (e.g. last night / eight years ago)
noSuggestions: Add a suspect’s motive and a false conclusion with an apparent supporting clue to get suggestions.
clean: No issues found in the entered structure.
saveError: Draft could not be saved. Check the fields.
issue_reference: “{0}”: a referenced node is missing from this investigation or has the wrong type. Select a valid node.
issue_duplicate: Duplicate identifier: {0}. Recreate one of the duplicate records.
issue_unstructured: This investigation has no structured plan yet. Fill in conclusions, discovery methods and time records to enable a full check.
issue_crimeMissing: Define the core event, affected person, motive, method and circumstances.
issue_requiredMissing: No required conclusion. Mark the facts needed to resolve the investigation.
issue_conclusionIncomplete: “{0}”: specify the conclusion and author’s truth for required facts.
issue_threeClues: “{0}” has {1} distinct clues. Consider creating {2} more to provide at least three. Fewer clues are accepted.
issue_entriesMissing: Choose at least one player entry point.
issue_endingsMissing: Choose at least one resolution node.
issue_methodMissing: “{0}”: describe how players discover this node. An empty action is not a discovery method.
issue_evidenceConflict: Confirmed clues both establish and refute a conclusion: {0}. Recheck reliability and logical roles.
issue_truthConflict: “{0}”: reachable confirmed clues establish the opposite of the author’s truth.
issue_requiredUnproven: “{0}”: players cannot establish this required fact. Add reachable independent evidence or correct its roles.
issue_unreachable: “{0}” is unavailable from the current entry points. Add a discovery method or link it to an accessible lead.
issue_unusedEvidence: “{0}”: this clue has no assigned logical role.
issue_consequenceMissing: “{0}”: the event has no described consequence.
issue_lockedCycle: Closed prerequisite cycle: {0}. Add an independent entry into the chain.
issue_deadEnd: “{0}”: the reachable branch ends without a resolution, required fact or refutation. Add a useful lead.
issue_deadCycle: This reachable loop has no useful exit: {0}. Add a route to a resolution or a meaningful conclusion.
issue_bottleneck: “{0}”: losing this node blocks a currently reachable ending or required fact. Consider an independent route.
issue_analysisLimit: This plan exceeds the exhaustive analysis budget. Some counterfactual or temporal checks are incomplete; split the plan into smaller investigations.
issue_timeIncomplete: “{0}”: specify the period, location and participants to check chronology.
issue_timeRange: Invalid time range or gap: {0}. The lower bound must not exceed the upper bound.
issue_timeMissing: “{0}”: no structured time record. Add one if its timing matters.
issue_orderReference: “{0}”: a temporal constraint references missing records or different periods.
issue_temporalCycle: No possible chronology satisfies these confirmed times and ordering constraints: {0}.
issue_alibiConflict: A confirmed alibi conflicts with presence or travel time: {0}.
issue_presenceConflict: A person cannot occupy these places within the confirmed time and travel limits: {0}.
issue_jointPresenceConflict: These confirmed presences and alibis cannot fit into one chronology: {0}. Recheck their ranges, durations and travel limits.
issue_timeAmbiguous: “{0}”: uncertain times allow both compatible and conflicting placements. Narrow the ranges or add ordering constraints.
issue_disputedTime: “{0}”: this time is disputed. It is retained as testimony and does not establish the factual chronology.
issue_versionIncomplete: “{0}”: specify the suspect, motive, explanation and a conclusion whose author’s truth is false.
issue_versionUnsupported: “{0}”: add an apparent supporting clue with a logical explanation.
issue_versionUncleared: “{0}”: players have no established refutation of this false version.
